lessons.title: The Millennial Man
lessons.description: This lesson uses the dream in Daniel's second chapter to introduce biblical prophecy. It explores the statue's parts and the sequence of kingdoms they represent. The study follows the vision toward the establishment of God's lasting kingdom. It connects the course of history with confidence in God's knowledge of the future. Readers are invited to consider where human power ends and divine rule begins.

lessons.title: Back to Jerusalem
lessons.description: This lesson introduces principles for understanding the Bible. It encourages careful comparison of passages rather than dependence on isolated phrases. The study connects fruitful reading with a willingness to learn and respond. Its focus is developing an approach grounded in Scripture's own explanations. Readers are encouraged to apply those methods throughout the series.

lessons.title: The Coming King
lessons.description: This lesson explores the promise and manner of Christ's return. It compares biblical descriptions with ideas that can obscure the event. The study considers what Jesus' coming means for His people. It connects the future hope with faith and preparation in the present. Readers are invited to build confidence in the Bible's account of that return.

lessons.title: The Rebellious Prince
lessons.description: This lesson uses the theme of a prince's rebellion to examine the origin of evil. It traces the conflict back to Satan's fall and his opposition to God. The study considers how rebellion affected humanity. It also asks what freedom and responsibility reveal about God's character. Readers are encouraged to view suffering within the Bible's larger conflict story.

lessons.title: The Supreme Sacrifice
lessons.description: This lesson connects Abraham's willingness to offer Isaac with the sacrifice of Jesus. It considers the meaning of trust and the cost of redemption. The study presents the story as an illustration of God's provision for humanity. It relates the rescue of Isaac to the promise of salvation through Christ. Readers are invited to consider a personal response to that love.

lessons.title: The Law of the King
lessons.description: This lesson examines God's law and its enduring place in a life of faith. It discusses the commandments as expressions of divine principles. The study connects obedience with love, loyalty, and the blessings of God's guidance. It challenges the view that following Christ makes the law irrelevant. Readers are encouraged to examine what honoring the King means in practice.

lessons.title: Bricks Without Straw
lessons.description: This lesson uses Israel's forced labor in Egypt to introduce the importance of Sabbath rest. It examines the biblical day of worship and its connection with creation. The study considers the tension between unrelenting labor and time dedicated to God. Its message connects liberation with the freedom to obey and worship. Readers are invited to examine the Sabbath's role in their own lives.

lessons.title: The Glorious Kingdom
lessons.description: This lesson explores the Bible's description of God's future kingdom. It considers the restored earth and life without suffering or death. The study presents that hope through the promises of Scripture. It connects the kingdom to God's purpose of dwelling with His people. Readers are encouraged to look beyond present hardship toward lasting restoration.

lessons.title: The Witch of Endor
lessons.description: This lesson examines Saul's visit to the witch of Endor. It asks whether the appearance he encountered was truly the dead prophet Samuel. The study compares the story with biblical teaching about death and forbidden spiritual practices. It connects the issue with the danger of deceptive supernatural experiences. Readers are encouraged to test claims about communication with the dead against Scripture.

lessons.title: Cities of Ash
lessons.description: This lesson uses the destruction of the cities of the plain to explore final punishment. It examines the Bible's imagery of fire and the removal of evil. The study challenges the idea of endless conscious torment. It connects the end of sin with God's justice and the restoration of peace. Readers are invited to compare its interpretation with the passages presented.

lessons.title: A River of Life
lessons.description: This lesson explains baptism and its relationship to a new life with Jesus. It studies the biblical meaning of being cleansed and beginning again. The discussion considers faith, commitment, and baptism by immersion. It connects the outward act with an inward response to God. Readers are encouraged to understand the decision before making it.

lessons.title: Resting the Land
lessons.description: This lesson explores the thousand years described in Revelation. It considers the earth's condition after the return of Jesus. The study discusses Satan's confinement and the sequence of resurrections. It also follows the events that close the millennium. Readers can examine how the lesson connects final judgment with the eventual restoration of the earth.

lessons.title: Bowing to Babylon
lessons.description: This lesson draws on the refusal to bow before Babylon's image. It explores faithfulness when religious demands are enforced through political power. The study connects that story with prophetic warnings about future worship conflicts. It emphasizes trust in God when obedience brings opposition. Readers are encouraged to develop convictions that do not depend on public approval.

lessons.title: The Mark of Cain
lessons.description: This lesson uses Cain's story to introduce questions about loyalty, worship, and a distinguishing mark. It connects those themes with Revelation's contrast between the seal of God and the mark of the beast. The study examines the role of authority in deciding whom to obey. It presents the author's interpretation of the final conflict over worship. Readers are encouraged to consider the convictions underlying their religious choices.

lessons.title: A Heavenly Model
lessons.description: This lesson introduces the sanctuary as a model of Christ's saving work. It examines how earthly services illustrate heavenly realities. The study connects sacrifice, priesthood, and forgiveness with Jesus. It encourages readers to understand the structure's purpose rather than regard it as an obsolete ritual system. The lesson provides a foundation for exploring Christ's ministry in heaven.

lessons.title: Cleansing the Temple
lessons.description: This lesson examines the cleansing of the sanctuary in Daniel's prophecy. It connects the earthly temple imagery with Christ's heavenly ministry. The study considers the time periods presented in Daniel's eighth and ninth chapters. Its interpretation places those prophecies within the Adventist understanding of judgment. Readers are encouraged to follow both the symbolism and the timing in Scripture.

lessons.title: A Tale of Two Women
lessons.description: This lesson contrasts two women used as symbols in Revelation. It examines the faithful church portrayed in the twelfth chapter. The study considers the characteristics that identify God's people before Christ returns. It connects faithfulness with biblical truth and obedience. Readers are invited to evaluate religious communities through the prophetic picture presented.

lessons.title: Windows of Heaven
lessons.description: This lesson explores tithing and the stewardship of money. It considers the promise associated with the windows of heaven in Malachi. The study connects returning tithe with acknowledging God's ownership. It also asks how trust and generosity shape a believer's priorities. Readers are encouraged to examine the spiritual meaning of their financial choices.

lessons.title: The Daughter’s Dance
lessons.description: This lesson studies Revelation's portrayal of Babylon and her related religious powers. It uses the theme of a daughter's influence to introduce the dangers of spiritual compromise. The study examines the identity and message of the symbolic woman. It connects those symbols with the call to leave religious confusion. Readers are encouraged to compare the lesson's interpretation with Scripture.

lessons.title: Ten Times Wiser
lessons.description: This lesson explores biblical health principles through the experience of Daniel and his companions. It considers the relationship between physical habits and spiritual faithfulness. The study discusses choices that support responsible care of the body. Its message treats health as part of Christian stewardship. Readers are encouraged to examine how their everyday habits reflect their commitments.

lessons.title: Voice in the Wilderness
lessons.description: This lesson explores how God's people can live differently from the surrounding world. It considers the relationship between inward faith and outward habits. The study connects a distinctive Christian witness with practical choices. Its focus is faithfulness rather than simply following social expectations. Readers are invited to examine whether their daily conduct reflects their relationship with God.

lessons.title: Proving the Prophets
lessons.description: This lesson presents biblical tests for evaluating prophets. It considers how truth, conduct, and consistency with Scripture help distinguish genuine messages. The study warns against accepting claims solely because they appear impressive. It connects spiritual discernment with careful examination of evidence. Readers are encouraged to apply those tests rather than rely on popularity or personal feeling.

lessons.title: A Jar of Oil
lessons.description: This lesson uses the widow's multiplying oil to explore the Holy Spirit's work. It discusses the Spirit's identity, guidance, and gifts. The study gives particular attention to the biblical gift of tongues and its purpose. It also considers the relationship between receiving the Spirit and responding to God's will. Readers are invited to seek a Spirit-filled life grounded in Scripture.

lessons.title: Above the Crowd
lessons.description: This lesson explores how believers can remain faithful amid social pressure. It considers the courage required to follow God when others choose differently. The study connects Christian commitment with practical decisions about loyalty and influence. Its message encourages readers to respond to truth rather than be directed by the crowd. Readers are invited to place their relationship with Jesus above public expectations.
